scenarios.title: Adopt a database that already has a schema
scenarios.tagline: Record the history a database already earned, and let the operator carry on from there.
scenarios.learn: How baseline proves a database matches its migrations before recording anything, and what it refuses.
events: # This database already has a shipments table and three rows. An application put them there.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -c "SELECT * FROM shipments ORDER BY id"
# It has no Ptah history. There is no revision table at all.
# The artifact the operator will run holds two migrations, published from these files.
# Baseline reads the same files. Hand them to the cluster, where it runs with the executor.
# Baseline through version 2 is refused. The shadow has a carrier column this database lacks.
BASELINE_VERSION=2 demo/bin/lab manifest adopt-baseline "$(cat demo/.lab/adopt-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
error: baseline shadow check failed: missing column shipments.carrier
# A refused baseline records nothing. There is still no revision table.
# This database is at release 1, so baseline through version 1.
BASELINE_VERSION=1 demo/bin/lab manifest adopt-baseline "$(cat demo/.lab/adopt-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# The history records version 1, and the rows are the rows it had.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -tAc "SELECT version, state FROM schema_migrations"
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -tAc "SELECT id, reference FROM shipments ORDER BY id"
# Now the resource. It reads that history, and plans version 2 alone.
APPLY=OnApproval demo/bin/lab manifest shipments "$(cat demo/.lab/adopt-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# Version 1 is history, so it is not offered. Approve the plan for version 2.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get ptahmigration shipments -o json > demo/.lab/migration.json
# Version 2 ran on the rows the application wrote, and the history carries on from there.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" exec deploy/demo-psql -- psql -tAc "SELECT version, state FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version"
"SELECT id || ' ' || reference || ' ' || carrier FROM shipments ORDER BY id"

scenarios.title: Recover a MySQL migration that stopped halfway
scenarios.tagline: DDL that committed, a run nobody can retry, and a repair decided by what the database holds.
scenarios.learn: How to find out what a partial MySQL migration left behind before choosing how to repair it.
events: # Release 1 creates the table on the lab's MySQL, and this resource applies it on its own.
APPLY=Always demo/bin/lab manifest deliveries "$(cat demo/.lab/deliveries-1-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# Three deliveries arrive. The next release has to keep them.
"INSERT INTO deliveries VALUES (1, 'D-100'), (2, 'D-200'), (3, 'D-300'); SELECT * FROM deliveries"
# Release 2 adds a status, fills it, then constrains it, naming a column that is not there.
-- Adds a status, fills it, and then constrains it. The constraint names a
-- column that does not exist, so the third statement fails after the first two
-- have committed: MySQL commits each DDL statement on its own.
ALTER TABLE deliveries ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16);
ALTER TABLE deliveries ADD CONSTRAINT deliveries_status_known CHECK (statuz IN ('open', 'closed'));
# Point the resource at release 2, and approve the plan it publishes.
APPLY=OnApproval demo/bin/lab manifest deliveries "$(cat demo/.lab/deliveries-2-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# The plan holds version 2 alone. Approve it by name, UID and fingerprint.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get ptahmigration deliveries -o json > demo/.lab/deliveries.json
# The run stopped partway. The resource records it and will not run anything until it is settled.
# First, what committed. The column exists and every row was filled.
# The revision table agrees. Version 2 stopped after two of its three statements.
"SELECT CONCAT('version ', version, ': ', applied, ' of ', total, ' statements, ', state) FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version"
# This database is disposable, so undo both statements. A real one needs its changes judged first.
"ALTER TABLE deliveries DROP COLUMN status; DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version = 2"
# Point the resource at release 1, which ends before the migration that failed.
APPLY=OnApproval demo/bin/lab manifest deliveries "$(cat demo/.lab/deliveries-1-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# Its next reading finds nothing to apply, and that reading is what clears the record.
# Release 3 carries the corrected migration. Point the resource at it.
APPLY=OnApproval demo/bin/lab manifest deliveries "$(cat demo/.lab/deliveries-3-digest)" | kubectl apply -f -
# Its plan holds the corrected version 2. Approve it the same way.
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get ptahmigration deliveries -o json > demo/.lab/deliveries.json
# All three statements ran this time, and the three deliveries are still there.
"SELECT CONCAT('version ', version, ': ', applied, ' of ', total, ' statements, ', state) FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;
SELECT CONCAT(id, ' ', reference, ' ', status) FROM deliveries ORDER BY id"
